title: HeaderMapNode: structured CBOR header map in ArticleRootNode
description:
Why: RFC 822/5322 headers are currently stored only as a raw byte block (header_cid, RAW codec 0x55), which is opaque to IPLD tooling. Adding a structured DAG-CBOR map block alongside the raw bytes enables ipfs dag get traversal of individual headers, lets Corundum read article metadata (subject, from, date) without a custom parser, and aligns with IPLD best practices. The raw bytes block is kept for wire-format fidelity and DKIM/S-MIME signature re-verification.

Schema change: add header_map_cid (DAG-CBOR CIDv1, codec 0x71) to ArticleRootNode after header_cid. No schema_version bump — no production instances exist yet, so this is part of the initial schema definition.

HeaderMapNode is BTreeMap<String, HeaderValue> where HeaderValue is untagged-serde enum Single(String) | Multi(Vec<String>). Header names are lowercased. Single occurrence -> string. Multiple occurrences -> array. Date-bearing headers (date, injection-date, nntp-posting-date, expires) are transformed to RFC 3339. If a date header cannot be parsed, the raw string is stored as fallback. All other header values are RFC 2047 decoded to UTF-8.
design: Option A: keep header_cid (raw bytes, RAW 0x55) for wire fidelity + add header_map_cid (DAG-CBOR 0x71) for IPLD traversal. BTreeMap for deterministic key ordering. serde untagged enum for heterogeneous string/array values. Date transformation oracle: Python email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime(). Fallback: unparseable dates stored as raw strings.
